description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and Accuracy, comparing three different metrics: a metric represented by a blue line, Δ Accuracy represented by an orange dashed line, and Initial Accuracy represented by a green dashed line. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence," with a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, and tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy," with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, and tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The blue line starts at approximately 0.9 on the y-axis at an Initial Confidence of 0.86 and remains relatively steady, ending at around 0.96 at an Initial Confidence of 1.00. The orange dashed line representing Δ Accuracy begins at around 0.3 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86, decreases to a minimum of approximately 0.05 at an Initial Confidence of 0.95, and then slightly increases to around 0.15 at an Initial Confidence of 1.00. The green dashed line representing Initial Accuracy starts at about 0.7 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86 and generally increases to around 0.93 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99 before decreasing to approximately 0.75 at an Initial Confidence of 1.00.
